chunks: And it was narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya from Hudhayfah ibn Mansur from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them both) that they said:
"The prayer during travel is two rak'ahs; there is nothing (extra prayer) before them or after them."

All these narrations indicate the elaboration of what was mentioned in the book, and I, by the will of God, will complete the discussion on the obligation of Qasr (shortening prayer) subsequently, if God wills.
ai.seo_question: What is the number of rak'ahs for prayer during travel and are there extra prayers before or after it?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) via Safwan ibn Yahya explicitly defines the travel prayer as strictly two rak'ahs, eliminating any supererogatory (nafl) prayers before or after it during the journey. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on the completeness and sufficiency of the shortened prayer in travel, distinguishing it from the full four-rak'ah prayer performed at home. The scholar notes that these reports clarify the specific details of the shortened prayer, setting the stage for a further discussion on the obligation of *taqsir* (shortening).
